subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a core admin-scoped shell-to-Control-UI notification broadcast surface, or should this remain folded into broader notification architecture work?
rationale: The code can support a new RPC/event, but the permanent authorization, targeting, payload, abuse-control, and product UX boundary is a maintainer security/product decision rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Design a core notify contract
options.body: Add an explicit CLI, Gateway RPC/event, Control UI handler, tests, and docs after defining admin scope, payload shape, rate limits, and delivery semantics.

options.title: Fold into broader UI notifications
options.body: Keep this issue open but make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 the design umbrella for the toast system before adding a shell entry point.

options.title: Defer to existing surfaces
options.body: Decline a new core command and document supported alternatives such as Web Push tests, system events, or plugin-defined broadcasts where appropriate.

recommendation.title: Design a core notify contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit CLI, Gateway RPC/event, Control UI handler, tests, and docs after defining admin scope, payload shape, rate limits, and delivery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested decision crosses the system CLI and Gateway broadcast/security boundary where his feature-history commits are strongest.
